accepted.title: Slice-ribbon question for flat knots
accepted.standalone_text: Is every oriented flat knot that is slice also ribbon? Slice means it bounds a properly immersed disk in a compact oriented 3-manifold whose boundary is the supporting oriented surface, equivalently it admits a connected genus-zero slice movie. Ribbon here means a slice movie with flat Reidemeister moves, saddles and deaths and no births, as in Chen’s Definition 2.34; it does not mean Turaev’s stronger symmetric-Gauss-diagram condition.
scope_notes: This question is about closed flat knots and Chen’s movie definition of ribbon.
Silver–Williams’ slice long flat knot that is not strongly ribbon does not refute this question.
accepted.status_evidence: Reaffirmed as Problem 5.3 in the current FlatKnotInfo author paper.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

definitions.flat_knot: An oriented flat knot is a stable homotopy class of a generically immersed oriented circle in an oriented surface; equivalently an oriented planar diagram with flat and virtual crossings modulo flat/virtual Reidemeister moves and detours.
definitions.slice_and_ribbon: A slice flat knot is represented by the boundary of a properly immersed disk in a compact oriented 3-manifold whose boundary is the supporting surface. Equivalently it has a connected genus-zero slice movie. Ribbon means a slice movie with flat Reidemeister moves, saddles and deaths and no births (Definition 2.34). This is different from Turaev’s strong-ribbon symmetry condition.
definitions.arrow_polynomial: For an oriented n-crossing diagram D, resolve each flat crossing by the oriented and disoriented smoothings of Figure 4.1. After cusp reductions, a state S with components carrying 2j_i remaining cusps contributes (−2)^{|S|−1}∏K_{j_i}, with K₀=1. The invariant is Ā(α)=(−1)^nΣ_S(−2)^{|S|−1}∏K_{j_i}∈Z[K₁,K₂,…] (finite polynomials). The cusp cancellation is the Figure 4.1 rule; it is not cancellation of arbitrary pairs of cusps.
definitions.long_group: A long flat knot is an oriented 1-tangle modulo flat/virtual moves, or a linear Gauss diagram. Connected sum is concatenation. A long knot is slice if its closure is slice. α and β are concordant when the closure of (−α*)#β is slice, where − reverses the interval and * reverses the surface orientation. FC is this group, with inverse [−α*].

accepted.title: Realization of normalized flat arrow polynomials
accepted.standalone_text: Which finite polynomials f∈Z[K₁,K₂,…] occur as the normalized flat arrow polynomial Ā(α) of an oriented flat knot α? For an n-crossing diagram D of α, Ā(α)=(−1)^nΣ_S(−2)^{|S|−1}∏_i K_{j_i}: S runs through its oriented/disoriented smoothing states, |S| is the number of state components, and the i-th component has 2j_i cusps after the flat-arrow cusp reductions (K₀=1).
scope_notes: Normalization is necessary to make this a question about knots rather than diagram parity. The source says flat arrow polynomial; its invariant is the normalized version.
The domain is knots (one component), not arbitrary flat links. The condition f(K_i=1)=1 is only a necessary calibration, not a realization theorem.
definition_locations: Definition 4.1, Figure 4.1 and Proposition 4.2, printed pp.47–49 / PDF pp.56–58
accepted.status_evidence: Reaffirmed as Problem 6.15 in the current FlatKnotInfo author paper.

accepted.title: Commutativity of the long flat-knot concordance group
accepted.standalone_text: Is the concordance group FC of oriented long flat knots abelian? Its multiplication is concatenation α#β. A long flat knot is slice when its closure is slice, and α is concordant to β when the closure of (−α*)#β is slice, where − reverses the interval orientation and * reverses the supporting surface orientation. Equivalently, are α#β and β#α concordant for every pair of oriented long flat knots?
scope_notes: LONG is essential: connected sum of closed flat knots is not a well-defined group operation.
The virtual-knot concordance group VC is known to be nonabelian, and the graded-based-matrix group FG is abelian. Neither fact decides FC.
accepted.status_evidence: The thesis states the question; the current author paper §5.3 still identifies commutativity of the long-flat-knot concordance group as a problem. No located later resolution in targeted searches.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

accepted.title: Large-coupling entropy-production ratio for harmonic Gaussian thermostats
accepted.standalone_text: Let (M,g) be a closed connected oriented surface of genus at least two with strictly negative Gaussian curvature, and let θ be a fixed nonzero harmonic real 1-form. Put λ(x,v)=θ_x(v), and let φ_t^τ be the Anosov flow generated by F_τ=X+τλV on SM for τ>0. For its unique SRB probability measure μ_τ, define e_τ=−∫_{SM}V(τλ)dμ_τ and h_τ=h_{μ_τ}(φ_1^τ), the metric entropy of the time-one map. Is e_τ/h_τ→+∞ as τ→+∞?
scope_notes: The SRB measure varies with τ; θ is nonzero and fixed, and g has K_g<0. Removing either condition changes the question.
Entropy production and metric entropy are distinct quantities. The former uses phase-space divergence; this is not a question about ordinary thermodynamic entropy.
§2.3.3 is acknowledged as joint work with Yann Chaubet; the thesis author remains Javier Echevarría Cuesta.
definition_locations: Definition 2.2.18 and Proposition 2.2.22, printed pp.37–38 / held PDF pp.46–47
accepted.status_evidence: Explicit thesis question; the current author publication list and targeted fresh searches provide no located resolution. This is bounded status evidence, not a proof that no resolution exists.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

definitions.thermostat: M is a smooth closed connected oriented Riemannian surface, SM its unit tangent bundle, X its geodesic vector field, V the generator of fibre rotations, H=[V,X], and λ∈C∞(SM,R). The thermostat flow φ_t is generated by F=X+λV, equivalently ∇_{γ̇}γ̇=λ(γ,γ̇)Jγ̇ at unit speed, with J positive rotation by π/2.
definitions.projectively_Anosov: The induced derivative P_t on T(SM)/RF has a continuous invariant splitting into line bundles E_s⊕E_u and constants C≥1, 0<ρ<1 such that ||P_t|E_s(v)|| ||P_{−t}|E_u(φ_t(v))||≤Cρ^t for t≥0. This is domination; the question does not assume separate contraction and expansion.
definitions.conjugate_points: The thermostat exponential map exp_x^λ(tv)=πφ_t(x,v) is singular at a nonzero tangent vector; no conjugate points means all these maps are local diffeomorphisms away from zero.
definitions.cotangent_Green_bundles: Let β be dual to H in the frame (X,H,V), and H*(v)=Rβ(v). On a no-conjugate-points thermostat, G_s*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_t)^* H*(φ_t(v)) and G_u*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_{−t})^* H*(φ_{−t}(v)); limits are of lines in T_v*(SM). These are the thesis cotangent Green bundles, not an unqualified tangent-bundle replacement.
definitions.curvatures: κ₀=K_g∘π−Hλ+λ², K_thermostat=κ₀+F(Vλ), and κ̃=κ₀+F(Vλ)/2−(Vλ)²/4. A magnetic system has Vλ=0. Do not replace κ̃ by K_thermostat.
definitions.source_definitions: Thesis §2.2, printed pp.23–38 / held PDF pp.32–47; §5.1.2, printed pp.84–87 / held PDF pp.93–96; equations (2.13), (5.4).

accepted.title: Conjugate points in projectively Anosov thermostats
accepted.standalone_text: Do there exist a smooth closed connected oriented Riemannian surface (M,g) and λ∈C∞(SM,R) such that the thermostat flow F=X+λV is projectively Anosov (its normal derivative has a dominated splitting into two invariant line bundles) but has a conjugate point, meaning that some thermostat exponential map exp_x^λ(tv)=πφ_t(x,v) is singular at a nonzero tangent vector?
scope_notes: No reversibility or nonwandering-set restriction is imposed. General projectively Anosov flows on SM need not be thermostat flows.
The source sibling D(M,g)⊆B(M,g) is exactly the universal negation of this existence question and should be merged, not numbered separately.
accepted.status_evidence: Retained in Thermostats without conjugate points, §1.3. Creation Theorem 1.2 is confined to reversible flows on their nonwandering sets and leaves this full question open.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

accepted.title: Non-Anosov projectively Anosov thermostats in genus at least two
accepted.standalone_text: Do there exist a smooth closed connected oriented Riemannian surface (M,g) of genus at least two and λ∈C∞(SM,R) for which the thermostat flow F=X+λV is projectively Anosov (its normal derivative has a dominated splitting into two invariant line bundles), but is not Anosov (it has no uniformly contracting and expanding strong stable/unstable splitting)?
scope_notes: The thesis and successor construct examples on the torus. Those examples do not satisfy the genus-at-least-two condition.
A construction of a general projectively Anosov flow on a hyperbolic 3-manifold is not enough: this flow must be X+λV on the surface unit tangent bundle.
accepted.status_evidence: Retained in Thermostats without conjugate points, §1.3; its torus construction is outside this target.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

accepted.title: Curvature rigidity from everywhere-collapsed magnetic Green bundles
accepted.standalone_text: Let (M,g) be a smooth closed connected oriented Riemannian surface, λ∈C∞(SM,R) satisfy Vλ=0, and φ_t be the magnetic thermostat flow F=X+λV without conjugate points. Put H=[V,X] and κ₀=K_g∘π−Hλ+λ². Must κ₀ vanish identically if its cotangent stable and unstable Green lines G_s*(v) and G_u*(v) agree for every v∈SM? Here G_s*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_t)^*Rβ(φ_t(v)) and G_u*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_{−t})^*Rβ(φ_{−t}(v)), with β dual to H in (X,H,V).
scope_notes: There is no κ₀≤0 or no-focal-points hypothesis. Equality is at every unit vector, not just almost everywhere.
This is the magnetic restriction of the converse direction in Question 5.1.18. The two labelled problems have different complete scopes; integration should disclose this relation.
accepted.status_evidence: Retained in Thermostats without conjugate points, §1.3. Corollary 1.10 adds κ₀≤0; the June 2026 entropy rigidity Theorem B adds absence of focal points. Neither is the exact target.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

accepted.title: Everywhere Green-bundle collapse and damped thermostat curvature
accepted.standalone_text: For a smooth thermostat F=X+λV on the unit tangent bundle of a closed connected oriented Riemannian surface, put H=[V,X] and κ̃=K_g∘π−Hλ+λ²+F(Vλ)/2−(Vλ)²/4. Is κ̃≡0 equivalent to the thermostat having no conjugate points and G_s*(v)=G_u*(v) for every v∈SM? The cotangent Green lines are G_s*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_t)^*Rβ(φ_t(v)) and G_u*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_{−t})^*Rβ(φ_{−t}(v)), where β is dual to H in (X,H,V).
scope_notes: The explicit no-conjugate-points clause unpacks the source’s domain for Green bundles; it is not an additional intended restriction. Source Theorem 5.1.1 with p=Vλ/2 already implies no conjugate points if κ̃=0.
The known measure-almost-everywhere equivalence under κ̃≤0 does not supply the everywhere equivalence.
Use κ̃, not the distinct thermostat curvature K_thermostat=κ₀+F(Vλ).
accepted.status_evidence: Retained in Thermostats without conjugate points, §1.3. Theorem 1.9(b) has a sign assumption and an almost-everywhere conclusion.
accepted.dedup_result: No exact or semantic numbered duplicate found in the full 4,800-question scan and related-family manual review.

definitions.thermostat: M is a smooth closed connected oriented Riemannian surface, SM its unit tangent bundle, X its geodesic vector field, V the generator of fibre rotations, H=[V,X], and λ∈C∞(SM,R). The thermostat flow φ_t is generated by F=X+λV, equivalently ∇_{γ̇}γ̇=λ(γ,γ̇)Jγ̇ at unit speed, with J positive rotation by π/2.
definitions.projectively_Anosov: The induced derivative P_t on T(SM)/RF has a continuous invariant splitting into line bundles E_s⊕E_u and constants C≥1, 0<ρ<1 such that ||P_t|E_s(v)|| ||P_{−t}|E_u(φ_t(v))||≤Cρ^t for t≥0. This is domination; the question does not assume separate contraction and expansion.
definitions.conjugate_points: The thermostat exponential map exp_x^λ(tv)=πφ_t(x,v) is singular at a nonzero tangent vector; no conjugate points means all these maps are local diffeomorphisms away from zero.
definitions.cotangent_Green_bundles: Let β be dual to H in the frame (X,H,V), and H*(v)=Rβ(v). On a no-conjugate-points thermostat, G_s*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_t)^* H*(φ_t(v)) and G_u*(v)=lim_{t→∞}(d_vφ_{−t})^* H*(φ_{−t}(v)); limits are of lines in T_v*(SM). These are the thesis cotangent Green bundles, not an unqualified tangent-bundle replacement.
definitions.curvatures: κ₀=K_g∘π−Hλ+λ², K_thermostat=κ₀+F(Vλ), and κ̃=κ₀+F(Vλ)/2−(Vλ)²/4. A magnetic system has Vλ=0. Do not replace κ̃ by K_thermostat.
definitions.source_definitions: Thesis §2.2, printed pp.23–38 / held PDF pp.32–47; §5.1.2, printed pp.84–87 / held PDF pp.93–96; equations (2.13), (5.4).
